resolved_by: The Supreme Court resolved the split in County of Riverside v. McLaughlin, 500 U.S. 44 (1991), holding that a judicial probable cause determination within 48 hours of arrest will generally satisfy Gerstein's promptness requirement.
issue: How promptly after a warrantless arrest must a judicial officer make a probable cause determination to satisfy the Fourth Amendment under Gerstein?
provision: Gerstein v. Pugh, 420 U.S. 103 (1975); County of Riverside v. McLaughlin, 500 U.S. 44 (1991)
quote: The Court therefore granted certiorari to resolve a circuit split “as to what constitutes a ‘prompt’ probable cause determination under Gerstein.” Id. at 50.
